spans.s:
वैकक्ष वैकक्ष, अम्, n. (fr. वि-कक्ष), a
garland or string of flowers &c. worn over one
shoulder and under the other (like the sacrificial
thread); an upper garment, wrapper, mantle.

वैकक्षक or वैकक्षिक, अम्, n. a garland
or string of flowers (worn as a kind of scarf hanging
down below the hip, or like the sacrificial cord, over
the left shoulder and under the right arm).

वैकङ्क वैकङ्क, N. of a mythical moun-
tain.

वैकङ्कत वैकङ्कत, अस्, m. (fr. वि-कङ्कत),
the plant Flacourtia Sapida (= वृन्तिङ्कर).

वैकटिक वैकटिक, अस्, m. (fr. वेकट), a
jeweller.

वैकर्ण वैकर्ण, अस्, m. = वि-कर्ण, epithet
of the wind (as fond of large or hollow ears?).

वैकर्त वैकर्त, अस्, m. (fr. वि-कर्त), Ved.
one who cuts up a sacrificial victim, a butcher; a
particular part of a slaughtered animal (cut off and
given to the priests at a sacrifice).

वैकर्तन, अस्, m. ‘son of Vi-kartana or the
Sun,’ N. of Karṇa.

वैकर्म वैकर्म, अस्, m., N. of the Muni
Vātsya.

वैकल्प वैकल्प, अम्, n. (fr. वि-कल्प), du-
biousness, uncertainty, ambiguity, optionality, inde-
cision; [cf. अर्थ-व्˚.]

वैकल्पिक, अस्, ई, अम्, doubtful, dubious, uncer-
tain, admitting of difference of opinion, indetermi-
nate, alternative, optional (= वि-कल्पित).

वैकल्य वैकल्य, अम्, n. (fr. वि-कल), im-
perfection, incompleteness, impairedness, deficiency,
defect, mutilation, a defective or imperfect state of
any limb or organ, lameness; incompetency, insuf-
ficiency; agitation, flurry; non-existence.

वैकारिक वैकारिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. वि-कार),
modifying, a changer, modifier, (see वि-कार); mo-
dified; (अस्), m. a class of deities.
—वैकारिक-
बन्ध, अस्, m. (in the Sāṅkhya phil.) one of the
threefold forms of bondage, (see बन्ध, वि-कार.)

वैकाल वैकाल, अस्, m. (fr. वि-काल), even-
ing, afternoon, (वैकाले, loc. c. in the evening.)

वैकालिक, अस्, ई, अम्, occurring in or belonging
to the evening; (अम्), ind. in the afternoon.
वैकालीन, अस्, ई, अम्, = वैकालिक above.

वैकुण्ठ वैकुण्ठ, अस्, m. (fr. वि-कुण्ठ),
N. of Viṣṇu; of Kṛṣṇa; of Indra, (Indra Vaikuṇṭha
is regarded as the author of the hymns Ṛg-veda

-50); holy basil; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a particular
class of gods; (अम्), n. the paradise or heaven of
Vaikuṇṭha or Viṣṇu, (its site is variously described
as in the northern ocean or on the eastern peak of
mount Meru); talc.
—वैकुण्ठ-चतुर्दशी, f. the
fourteenth day of the light half of the month Kārt-
tika (sacred to Viṣṇu).
—वैकुण्ठ-पुरी, m., N.
of an author and commentator, (also called विष्णु-
पुरी.)
—वैकुण्ठ-लोक, अस्, m. the world of
Viṣṇu.
—वैकुण्ठ-वर्णन, अम्, n. a descrip-
tion of Vaikuṇṭha.

वैकृत वैकृत, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. वि-कृति), un-
dergoing change, changed (in mind or form); modi-
fied; (अम्), n. change, modification, alteration;
change of mind, aversion, disgust.
—वैकृत-सर्ग,
अस्, m. a kind or form of creation, (opposed to प्रा-
[]
कृत-सर्ग.)
—वैकृतापह (˚त-अप्˚), अस्, आ, अम्,
removing or preventing change.

वैकृतिक, अस्, ई, अम्, changed, modified, inci-
dental; (in the Sāṅkhya phil.) belonging to a Vi-
kāra, i. e. to an evolute or evolved principle, (see
वि-कार, प्र-कृति.)

वैकृत्य, अस्, आ, अम्, changed (in form or mind);
(अम्), n. change, alteration; aversion, disgust.

वैक्रान्त वैक्रान्त, अम्, n. (fr. वि-क्रान्त), a
kind of gem (= गो-नास, said to resemble a diamond
or burnt diamond; according to others, the common
loadstone or magnet).

वैक्लव वैक्लव, अम्, n. (fr. वि-क्लव), agi-
tation or distress of mind, bewilderment.

वैक्लव्य, अम्, n. confusion, agitation, distress,
affliction, despair, bewilderment, commotion, tumult.
